reason: The text demonstrates clear collaboration between the Israelite leadership (Moses and Aaron) and the people. When Moses calls the elders of Israel ('ויקרא משה לכל זקני ישראל') and instructs them to take animals and slaughter the Passover, the text explicitly states that 'the children of Israel went and did as YHWH commanded Moses and Aaron, so they did' (וילכו ויעשו בני ישראל כאשר צוה יהוה את משה ואהרן כן עשו). Throughout the passage, Moses and Aaron receive divine instructions together, perform miracles together, and lead the people in unified action toward liberation and worship. The people respond to leadership directives with coordinated obedience. However, this applies specifically to the Israelite community; the Egyptian example shows the opposite—Pharaoh resists collaboration with his own servants, who openly oppose his resistance to letting the people go.
